nodes.description: Constructor of the Rickle token contract that initializes symbol, name, decimals, total supply and pre-assigns the entire balance to a fixed address.
Returns the total token supply minus the balance held by the zero address.
Returns the token balance of a given account owner.
Transfers tokens from msg.sender to a recipient using safeSub/safeAdd balance updates.
Sets the allowance msg.sender grants to a spender without any double-spend checks.
Transfers tokens from one account to another, deducting the spender allowance computed via balances and allowed mappings.
Returns the remaining allowance a token owner has granted to a spender.
Sets allowance and then makes an external call to the spender contract's receiveApproval, enabling reentrancy.
Owner-only function that makes an external call to an arbitrary token contract to transfer out tokens held by this contract.
Owner-only function that stages a new owner address in newOwner.
Completes ownership transfer when called by the pending newOwner, setting owner and clearing newOwner.
Subtraction helper that requires b <= a before computing a - b.
Addition helper that requires the result to be >= a to prevent overflow.
Multiplication helper guarding against overflow.
Division helper that requires a non-zero divisor.
Address of the current contract owner, set from msg.sender in the constructor and used by onlyOwner checks.
Staged pending owner address used by the two-step ownership transfer.
Mapping of account address to token balance, mutated by transfer and transferFrom.
Nested mapping of owner to spender to allowance, mutated by approve, approveAndCall and transferFrom.
Total token supply assigned only in the constructor and read by totalSupply.
Caller-controlled address used for balances, allowances, ownership assignment and access checks.
External call to an arbitrary spender contract's receiveApproval after state updates, a reentrancy vector.
External call into an arbitrary token contract's transfer on behalf of the contract.
Arithmetic operations performed through SafeMath helpers where manual overflow/underflow guards are required.
Recipient address parameter of transfer.
Amount of tokens parameter of transfer.
Source account parameter of transferFrom whose balance is debited.
Spender address parameter of approve.
Arbitrary calldata forwarded to the spender's receiveApproval during the external call.
Candidate new owner address parameter stored in newOwner.
Arbitrary ERC20 token contract address targeted by the owner-only external call.

edges.reason: Constructor assigns owner from msg.sender, establishing the privileged owner account.
Constructor sets the total supply state variable.
Constructor pre-assigns the entire supply into the balances mapping.
msg.sender becomes the owner during construction, gating onlyOwner functions.
Transfer debits the balance of the caller msg.sender.
Approve records the allowance granted by the caller msg.sender.
TransferFrom consumes the allowance indexed by the caller msg.sender.
ApproveAndCall writes the allowance of the caller msg.sender.
msg.sender is used as the spender key when decrementing the allowed mapping.
acceptOwnership requires msg.sender to equal the staged newOwner before transferring ownership.
onlyOwner modifier on transferAnyERC20Token compares msg.sender against owner.
Recipient parameter controls which balance is credited in transfer.
Token amount parameter controls how much balance is moved in transfer.
From parameter selects which balance and allowance are debited in transferFrom.
Spender parameter is the key written into the allowed mapping by approve.
Data parameter is forwarded verbatim into the external receiveApproval call.
New owner parameter is stored into the newOwner state variable.
Token address parameter determines the target of the external transfer call.
transfer relies on SafeMath.safeSub to debited balances without underflow.
transfer relies on SafeMath.safeAdd to credit balances without overflow.
transferFrom uses safeSub for both the balance and allowance deductions.
transferFrom uses safeAdd to credit the recipient balance.
safeSub performs the actual subtraction arithmetic guarded by a require.
safeAdd performs the actual addition arithmetic guarded by an overflow require.
approve writes the allowance into the allowed mapping.
transferFrom decrements the spender allowance in the allowed mapping.
approveAndCall sets the allowance before performing the external call.
balanceOf reads an account balance from the balances mapping.
allowance reads the nested allowed mapping for owner and spender.
totalSupply reads the total supply state variable.
approveAndCall invokes receiveApproval on an untrusted spender contract after state changes, enabling reentrancy.
The untrusted receiveApproval callback can re-enter transfer, replaying balance updates before the call returns.
transferAnyERC20Token delegates to an external ERC20 transfer call.
The external transfer is directed to the owner address, transferring arbitrary tokens out.
transferOwnership writes the staged owner into the newOwner state variable.
acceptOwnership reads and then clears the newOwner state variable.
acceptOwnership promotes newOwner into the owner state variable, changing privileged control.

normalization_plan.reason: The destination address parameter only exists to feed the transfer function's balance credit and has no independent semantic identity.
The token amount parameter is a pure input to the transfer function's arithmetic and event emission.
The source account parameter only determines which balance and allowance keys are used inside transferFrom.
The spender parameter is solely the mapping key written by approve and should be folded into it.
The opaque data blob is only meaningful when forwarded into the untrusted receiveApproval external call, which is the core unsafe operation.
The candidate owner parameter is only consumed by the ownership transfer function that stores it.
The token address parameter exists purely to target the external ERC20 call, the core unsafe operation.
